g.text: Every write lands in one signed, hash-linked log in your bucket. Everything else reads it.
on other machines verify each object against your key;
a write shows up in about 140 ms (p50)
one row per change, committed every 60 s by default;
DuckDB, Spark and pyiceberg query it
a read-only graph as it stood at any instant;
it gives the same answer as SQL over the table
gone from memory at once, then from disk, the bucket
and the Iceberg files: all of it in 6.9 s in our S3 run
